goal.text: Turn weekly platform order exports into a finance-ready billing table.

refs.quote: The pipeline fetches orders, applies refunds, and renders the report.

mechanism_chain.text: Raw order events are pulled from the platform export.
Refunds are split into pre-shipment and post-shipment buckets.

refs.quote: `apply_refunds()` splits refunds into pre-shipment and post-shipment buckets

mechanism_chain.text: The weekly table renders from the split results; window correctness is assumed, not checked.

assumptions.text: The platform export covers exactly the requested window.

refs.quote: The platform export is assumed complete for the requested window

assumptions.if_wrong: weekly totals silently include or miss rows (probe saw 391 outside-window rows)

assumptions.text: Refund status is final once the export marks it settled.

refs.quote: Refund status is assumed final once the export marks it settled

assumptions.if_wrong: late refunds leak between weeks and totals drift

assumptions.text: The rate table in use is current for the report month.
assumptions.if_wrong: stale currency conversion silently misstates amounts

findings_explained.text: The 391 out-of-window rows measured by the probe mean weekly totals are computed over a fuzzy window, so 'numbers match the platform' is not yet a safe statement.
rate_for() falls back to the last dict entry for unknown months, so a stale table is used without error — the Known Debt is a real silent failure mode.

unknowns.text: Whether long windows get silently truncated by the export API.
unknowns.impact: weekly totals could be systematically low
unknowns.next_evidence: row-count parity check against platform UI for one week

unknowns.text: How often late refunds settle after the export marks them settled.
unknowns.impact: week-over-week totals may not be additive
unknowns.next_evidence: refund status changelog sample over 4 weeks
